text:
ops-bot: ALERT: Production SLO breach detected on streaming generate endpoints. p95 ~ 480ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 2.1s -> 7.4s over the last 10m. Error rate stable. Affected regions: us-west1, europe-west2. Potential root: cache miss spike. Paging oncall. #incident

eric-oncall: on it. moving to this thread. paging @sre-liz and @sam. what was the deploy window? :eyes:

sre-liz: saw a rollout 25m ago that touched prefix hashing in the cache key code (PR #4392). Telemetry shows cache hit-rate for streaming-prefixes dropped from 88% -> 6% around that time.

sam: confirmed — the prefix-hash function changed to include session_id bits. We expected graceful migration but looks like the key namespace changed entirely.

eric-oncall: that would cause a cold-cache storm. explains tail latency. are downstream caches (redis) evicted? memory metrics?

mike: redis cluster mem usage steady, evictions low. but redis miss rate for LRU counters spiked. perf logs show a lot more model inference calls hitting the runtime instead of cache.

sre-liz: adding snapshots:
```
# cache metrics (from /metrics/cache)
stream_prefix_hit_rate{env=\"prod\",region=\"us-west1\"} 0.062
stream_prefix_qps_miss{env=\"prod\",region=\"us-west1\"} 420.3
```

eric-oncall: thanks. immediate mitigation options? rollback prefix-hash change, rewarm cache, or throttle traffic + route to smaller model variant?

sam: rollback is simplest but PR is already in prod. rollback will restore old keys and hit-rate, but need deploy approval. can we do a quick config flip to accept both key formats?

sre-liz: we can enable legacy-key-compat in the serving layer for a short window. it's a config flag that tries old hash before new hash. low risk.

eric-oncall: do it. which service? key-service and streaming-proxy?

sre-liz: mainly streaming-proxy v2 and keygen-service. I'll push the flag to true in us-west1 and europe-west2.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started rollout of config flag 'legacy-key-compat' to streaming-proxy v2 in us-west1 by sre-liz.

sre-liz: rolled to 20% -> 50% -> 100% in us-west1. monitoring hit-rate...

mike: hit-rate recovering: 6% -> 42% within 4 minutes. p95 dropping from 1.8s -> 420ms. p99 still a little high ~1.6s.

eric-oncall: good. do same for europe-west2.

sam: europe rollout started.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Completed config rollout in europe-west2.

mike: europe hit-rate back to ~65%. p95 ~ 380ms, p99 ~ 900ms. still above SLO target for p99.

sre-liz: likely because of the rewarm backlog — cache warms gradually as requests hit legacy keys and get cached under new namespace. we should actively rewarm hot prefixes from logs to speed recovery.

eric-oncall: I can kick off a rewarm job with the top 5k prefixes from traffic last 24h. would that flood the runtime?
\sre-liz: rewarm can be throttled. we should run at 50 qps per region to not overload. also consider a temporary routing rule: direct tier-1 customers to dedicated cache-backed pool.

sam: initiating rewarm job: `./tools/warmer --src=access-logs --limit=5000 --rate=50 --regions=us-west1,europe-west2`

ops-bot: job-bot: Cache warmer job 7721 started (50 qps).

mike: monitoring: after ~12 minutes rewarm progress 33%. p99 dropped to 560ms.

cs-ana: CS update: two paying customers reported elevated latencies, one opened a ticket. informing them we have active mitigations and expect normal levels in ~20m.

eric-oncall: good note. we should also enable a temporary fallback model route for latency-sensitive tenants: route to model-small-1 (slightly lower quality) with cached responses prioritized. Sam, can you configure route?

sam: yes, adding routing policy for customer_tier == gold to prefer model-small-1. will propagate in 60s.

ops-bot: config-bot: Routing policy change applied to traffic router.

mike: p95/p99 now: us-west1 p95 320ms p99 420ms; europe p95 340ms p99 480ms. within SLO for p95 and getting p99 close to target.

eric-oncall: great. next steps: 1) keep legacy-key-compat for 24h, 2) prepare rollback PR for prefix-hash change (safer long-term), 3) add migration plan with gradual keybackfill and warmers, 4) postmortem and customer communication.

sre-liz: I'll open a revert PR and a follow-up with a migration toggled by gradual sampling. also will add cache hit-rate alert thresholds for >20% drop.

sam: will coordinate with SDK/devex to mark any change in hash key semantics in changelog.

eric-oncall: CS Ana, please send templated update to affected customers with ETA 2h and note mitigations done.

cs-ana: on it. sending updates now.

mike: adding incident tags: cause=prefix-key-migration, impact=latency-spike,p99-breach, mitigation=legacy-compat,cache-rewarm,routing-fallback

eric-oncall: we're currently in monitoring state. will keep this thread updated. set severity to Sev2.

ops-bot: Incident updated: Sev2, owner=eric-oncall, status=monitoring.

sre-liz: postmortem checklist: timestamped deploy that introduced change, linked PR #4392, timeline of hit-rate and latency, config flip timeline, rewarm job id 7721, revert PR #4405, SDK notice. I'll draft and link here.

eric-oncall: thanks. closing the active pager. if anything regresses ping this thread or escalate to Sev1. :thumbsup:

sam: ack.

cs-ana: customers updated. one follow-up ticket from enterprise A; we've offered a call.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Revert PR #4405 merged to main and queued for deploy (manual approval required).

eric-oncall: leave legacy-key-compat on until revert hits prod and we see stable hit-rate >80% and p99 < 500ms for 30m.

mike: noted. continuing to watch metrics and alerts.

sre-liz: will drop a postmortem draft in #postmortems by EOD with remediation items: safer key migration pattern, rolling compatibility, automated warmer, and alert tuning.

eric-oncall: thanks team. good rapid coordination.

ops-bot: Incident resolved: status=stable, closed_by=eric-oncall, closed_at=1770454721
